design: Use M0 as the explicit historical activity, volume, counterparty, and degree baseline.
Evaluate incremental gains rather than raw performance alone.
Include log-transformed counts and bounded composition measures.
Report performance by prespecified historical activity strata.
activity_volume_confound_controls.interpretation_warning: An improvement concentrated only in the highest-activity stratum should be described as conditional incremental utility, not general behavioral predictability.
activity_volume_confound_controls.residualized_sensitivity: As a secondary analysis, regress each target dimension on M0 predictions using training data only and test whether M1 or M2 predicts the remaining residual. This is not the primary analysis because residualization can amplify estimation noise.
activity_volume_confound_controls.result_dependent_choices: No volume adjustment, stratum boundary, or residualization method may be added after inspecting results.
activity_volume_confound_controls.stratified_reporting: Strata are fixed before results and are not used to select the primary conclusion.

cheapest_falsification_experiment.cost: No new event extraction, graph construction, matching, or feature materialization is required.
cheapest_falsification_experiment.design: Run the complete nested comparison using the already materialized feature and outcome tables, with June training, July development, and August test, using only M0 and M1.
cheapest_falsification_experiment.falsification_target: If M1 fails to improve over M0 on the preregistered August multivariate target under cluster-robust uncertainty, the temporal-signal claim is not supported.
cheapest_falsification_experiment.status: Recommended first-stage analysis and pre-analysis design choice.

concise_recommended_protocol.overall_recommendation: Proceed only as a blinded, preregistered, bounded pilot. The strongest defensible primary test is M1 versus M0 on the 7-day multivariate future-change target; M2_CORE versus M1 is secondary and should not be overinterpreted with only one held-out cutoff.
protocol: Use the existing 27,613-wallet by three-cutoff population and the existing discovery and future tables.
Require history activity and a nonempty score window; use fixed 7-day future change as primary and 30-day change as secondary.
Define a six-dimensional future-change target with training-only transforms and equal-weight multivariate standardized loss.
Compare M0, M1, and M2_CORE using the same ridge model, same preprocessing, and same tuning budget.
Train on June, tune on July, refit on June plus July, and test once on August.
Report repeated-wallet and unseen-wallet results separately.
Use wallet-cluster bootstrap intervals and fixed 2 percent improvement thresholds.
Run leakage, completeness, negative-control, and activity-stratified audits.
Do not use matching as the primary design.
Interpret any favorable result as preliminary incremental predictability, not confirmation; if the primary interval includes zero, record a no-go for the corresponding claim.

hypotheses.H0_M1_vs_M0: M1 has no lower expected out-of-sample loss than M0.
hypotheses.H0_M2_vs_M0: M2_CORE has no lower expected out-of-sample loss than M0.
hypotheses.H0_M2_vs_M1: M2_CORE has no lower expected out-of-sample loss than M1.
hypotheses.H1_M1_vs_M0: M1 has lower expected out-of-sample loss than M0.
hypotheses.H1_M2_vs_M0: M2_CORE has lower expected out-of-sample loss than M0.
hypotheses.H1_M2_vs_M1: M2_CORE has lower expected out-of-sample loss than M1.

estimand_and_hypotheses.interpretation_boundary: A positive result would support incremental predictability of future behavioral change, not causal inference, identity-level generalization, or any claim about an external behavioral category.
estimand_and_hypotheses.primary_estimand: Out-of-sample incremental predictive utility of M1 over M0, and M2_CORE over M1 and M0, measured on a predeclared multivariate future-change target at the August 2022 cutoff.
estimand_and_hypotheses.scientific_question: Whether pre-cutoff temporal and structural information improves prediction of future behavioral change beyond historical activity, volume, counterparty count, and degree.
secondary_estimands: Incremental predictive utility for each prespecified target dimension.
Performance on wallets not observed at any earlier cutoff.
Performance for the 7-day horizon versus the 30-day horizon.
estimand_and_hypotheses.threshold_status: All estimands, target definitions, feature memberships, evaluation splits, and decision thresholds are pre-analysis design choices. No result-dependent primary modification is permitted.

include: History event counts over 1-day, 7-day, and 30-day windows
History active days and active hours
Total incoming, outgoing, and self-event counts
Unique counterparty count and degree proxy
Native inflow, native outflow, and net native flow where available
M0.name: Historical activity and basic scale
M0.rationale: Defines the minimum historical activity, volume, counterparty, and degree baseline.

include: Inter-event gap median, mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum where at least two events exist
Prior-window versus score-window changes in event count, active days, counterparties, and event-family composition
Counterparty novelty, repeat, turnover, and growth from prior versus score windows
M1.name: M0 plus temporal information
M1.rationale: Tests whether temporal organization and recent change add information beyond level and scale.

include: Reciprocity-related counts and simple proportions available directly from the frozen feature table
Simple adjacent-event rapid-forwarding proxy, only if its exact construction is documented and reproducible without additional semantic assumptions
M2_CORE.name: M1 plus conservative structural information
M2_CORE.rationale: Tests structural incremental value using features already materially available and interpretable.

candidate_features: Validated temporal-cycle summaries that do not require semantic inference
M2_EXTENDED.exclusion_rule: Do not include asset-aware split or merge features, cross-asset quantity aggregation, unrestricted graph motifs, or features requiring semantic judgments not already validated.
M2_EXTENDED.inclusion_rule: Every feature must have a frozen SQL definition, leakage test, missingness rule, computational cost estimate, and documented interpretation before inclusion.
M2_EXTENDED.rationale: Avoids turning the extended model into an unconstrained feature-search exercise.
M2_EXTENDED.status: Optional secondary model only; not part of the primary claim unless frozen by a preregistered amendment before unblinding results.

feature_scaling.categorical_features: No unrestricted identifiers; only fixed low-cardinality event-family indicators are allowed.
feature_scaling.count_features: Use log1p before scaling where prespecified.
feature_scaling.numeric_features: Training-fold median imputation only where a feature is structurally missing, followed by training-fold scaling.

general_rules: All features must be computed from event_timestamp < cutoff_time.
All transformations, clipping, scaling, and imputation parameters are fit within each training fold.
No wallet address, counterparty identifier, unrestricted categorical ID, or future-derived field is allowed.
Each model receives the same rows, target, split, preprocessing framework, and tuning budget.

exclude: Any future outcome or future-derived normalization
Any field generated using rows at or after cutoff
Features selected by univariate association with future outcomes
Asset-aware split and merge features without a frozen semantic definition
Temporal cycles requiring additional unreviewed materialization
Exact reciprocity-change parity features unless independently validated and preregistered
features_to_exclude_or_freeze.status: All exclusions and freezes are pre-analysis choices.

circularity_and_confound_flags: The event-count and unique-counterparty components remain partly activity-related; this is intentional but must be interpreted as prediction of change rather than pure behavioral novelty.
A target based only on future total activity would be dominated by scale and would not answer the stated question; therefore composition and active-day dimensions are included.
If any future dimension is unavailable for a row because of incomplete observation, that row is excluded from the relevant prespecified analysis rather than imputed from future information.
The 30-day target can be statistically noisier and more dependent across cutoffs; it cannot replace the 7-day primary target.
non_circularity: The target uses only future outcomes and a previously observed reference window; candidate feature families do not define the target.
Target scaling, winsorization, and any missingness rules are fit on training data only.
The target is not selected according to model performance or observed target distributions at the test cutoff.
The scalar aggregate is defined before results and does not use model predictions.

primary_target_construction.composition_definition: Use prespecified bounded shares for native, token, internal, and external event families. Use additive smoothing fixed before analysis, with smoothing constant 0.5 events per category.
primary_target_construction.directional_variant: Retain the signed target vector for regression. Do not replace it with absolute changes for the primary model, because magnitude-only targets discard directional behavioral change.
primary_target_construction.scalar_surprise: The equal-weighted squared Euclidean norm of the training-standardized target vector, with each dimension contributing equally after training-only standardization.
primary_target_construction.standardization: Fit location and scale parameters using training cutoffs only. Apply those parameters unchanged to development and test rows. Winsorization, if used, is fixed at the training 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles and is not recomputed on later data.
target_vector: log1p(future event count) minus log1p(score-window event count)
log1p(future unique-counterparty count) minus log1p(score-window unique-counterparty count)
future active-day count minus score-window active-day count
future incoming-event share minus score-window incoming-event share
future outgoing-event share minus score-window outgoing-event share
future event-family composition contrasts minus score-window event-family composition contrasts

future_behavioral_surprise.recommendation: Use both a prespecified multivariate target and its scalar aggregate. Treat the multivariate target as primary for reporting and the scalar aggregate as the primary hypothesis-test statistic.

secondary_target_construction.definition: Construct the same target dimensions using a 30-day future window and a matched 30-day pre-cutoff reference window [t-30d,t), with training-only standardization.
secondary_target_construction.role: Secondary robustness analysis only; it is not used for feature selection, threshold selection, or primary conclusions.

future_behavioral_surprise.target_status: All target dimensions, windows, smoothing, scaling, and aggregation rules are pre-analysis design choices.

go_modify_no_go_rule.modification_rule: Any change to targets, windows, cutoffs, inclusion rules, features, model family, tuning budget, or thresholds requires a preregistered amendment before inspecting the affected results.
no_go_rule: If the confidence interval includes zero for the first-priority M1 versus M0 contrast, conclude no demonstrated incremental temporal signal in this pilot.
If M2_CORE does not improve over M1, conclude no demonstrated incremental structural signal.
If negative controls show comparable or larger gains than the intended features, invalidate the corresponding result pending audit.
If test-set completeness or feature provenance fails, do not interpret predictive results.
go_modify_no_go_rule.pilot_boundary: Because only one cutoff is held out, even a result meeting the go rule should be described as preliminary and should not be treated as a confirmed general effect.

primary_go_rule.condition: Proceed to a bounded positive interpretation only if M1 versus M0 has a test-set relative loss reduction of at least 2 percent, the 95 percent wallet-cluster bootstrap interval excludes zero, and the direction is consistent for at least four of the six primary target dimensions.

go_modify_no_go_rule.result_dependent_choices: No primary rule may be weakened, replaced, or selectively applied after results are known.

structural_go_rule.condition: Treat structural information as supported only if M2_CORE versus M1 has at least a 2 percent relative loss reduction, the 95 percent interval excludes zero, and the gain is not confined to a single target dimension.

identity_controls: Exclude anchor wallet address from all features.
Exclude raw counterparty identifiers and unrestricted categorical encodings.
Do not allow row-level random splits.
Audit whether any aggregate feature is effectively a wallet identifier through near-unique cardinality.
join_controls: Audit one-to-one or documented one-to-many joins.
Check that future rows cannot duplicate training features.
Hash and compare feature-row keys before and after joins.
Verify that cutoff timestamps and event timestamps use UTC consistently.
identity_and_temporal_leakage_controls.leakage_audit: Run a feature provenance report listing source table, maximum permitted timestamp, aggregation window, missingness rule, and transformation for every column.
temporal_controls: Enforce event_timestamp < cutoff_time in every discovery query.
Use half-open windows exactly as declared.
Fit all preprocessing only on earlier cutoffs.
Prevent future outcome columns from entering feature tables, joins, filters, normalizers, or eligibility logic.
Freeze model predictions before inspecting August target summaries beyond required QA.

phase_1_protocol_freeze: Register target definitions, feature manifests, split rules, model grid, metrics, resampling, and decision thresholds.
Create immutable analysis configuration with version hash.
Record the three cutoff timestamps and all half-open intervals.
phase_2_data_checks: Verify expected row counts for the discovery grid and feature table.
Verify one row per anchor-wallet and cutoff.
Check completeness through each future horizon.
Check duplicate event handling and join multiplicity.
phase_3_feature_checks: Generate a provenance manifest for every feature.
Check feature minimum, maximum, missingness, and cardinality using training data.
Verify that token quantities are not aggregated across assets.
Verify that no feature query references future outcomes.
phase_4_model_checks: Save June fits, July tuning losses, selected penalties, and August predictions.
Run a synthetic leakage test in which future columns are deliberately injected and confirm that the audit detects them.
phase_5_evaluation: Evaluate August once after all specifications are frozen.
Report primary, secondary, negative-control, and subgroup results.
Do not use August results to revise the primary specification.
implementation_plan_and_qa.qa_failure_rule: Any failed critical QA item blocks interpretation until resolved through a preregistered amendment.
reproducibility: Pin software and database query versions.
Record random seeds for any resampling.
Store row-key hashes and prediction hashes.

inclusion_and_observability_rules.anchor_population: Use the already declared 27,613-wallet by three-cutoff discovery grid without redesigning the population.
observability: Require complete event coverage through t+7d for the primary target and t+30d for the secondary target.
Do not censor or impute a future window merely because activity is zero.
Use the same inclusion rule at all cutoffs.
Report the number and proportion excluded by each rule and cutoff.
inclusion_and_observability_rules.primary_history_rule: Require at least one event in [t-30d,t).
inclusion_and_observability_rules.primary_score_rule: Require at least one event in [t-7d,t) for the primary change analysis.
inclusion_and_observability_rules.result_dependent_choices: No inclusion threshold may be changed after inspecting outcomes, model scores, or cutoff-specific distributions.
inclusion_and_observability_rules.sensitivity_status: These thresholds are pre-analysis design choices and are not selected by future outcomes.
inclusion_and_observability_rules.small_history_features: Features requiring at least two historical events receive an explicit structural-missing indicator and training-only imputation; they are not silently set to zero.

amendment_content: Freeze the revised specification before accessing affected outcomes.
Label amended analyses as secondary or exploratory unless the amendment occurs before any relevant result is viewed.
amendments_required_before_results: Changing any target window or target dimension.
Changing model family or tuning budget.
Changing inclusion, completeness, or decision thresholds.
Introducing a new negative control or subgroup as a confirmatory analysis.
limitations: Only three cutoff dates are available, yielding one strictly held-out temporal test point.
Repeated wallets create dependence and limit effective sample size.
The unseen-wallet analysis may have lower power and different selection composition.
Future activity and composition are measured observationally and may contain unobserved exposure differences.
The target includes activity-related dimensions despite explicit controls.
A linear model may miss nonlinear effects, while adding flexible models with three cutoffs risks overfitting.
The study estimates predictive association, not causality.
limitations_and_preregistration_amendmen.recommendation: Treat OW-010B as a bounded temporal-prediction pilot unless additional cutoffs are preregistered and collected before confirmatory claims.

matching_secondary_analysis.balance_rule: Declare failure if any prespecified covariate has absolute standardized mean difference greater than 0.10 after weighting or matching.
matching_secondary_analysis.method: If used, match or weight rows using pre-cutoff M0 covariates only, separately within cutoff and with wallet-cluster-aware diagnostics.
matching_secondary_analysis.outcome_use: Future outcomes are not used to construct, tune, or assess the matching procedure.
matching_secondary_analysis.overlap_rule: Declare failure if more than 10 percent of eligible rows lack a counterpart or usable weight under the fixed overlap rule.
matching_secondary_analysis.reporting: Report the unmatched analysis first and present matched results only as sensitivity evidence.
matching_secondary_analysis.role: Descriptive secondary analysis only; matching is not a primary design element.
matching_secondary_analysis.threshold_status: The 0.10 balance rule and 10 percent overlap rule are pre-analysis design choices.

baselines: Historical-reference baseline that predicts no change from the prior score window.
models_and_equal_budget.equal_budget: M0, M1, M2_CORE, and any preregistered M2_EXTENDED model use the same algorithm, same five penalty values, same preprocessing, same development set, same target, and same fitting calls.
models_and_equal_budget.model_selection_boundary: No model family, hyperparameter grid, or feature subset may be added to the primary analysis after August test results are inspected.
models_and_equal_budget.primary_model_family: Regularized multivariate linear regression using ridge penalty.
models_and_equal_budget.reason: It is interpretable, stable with correlated feature families, computationally simple, and directly comparable across nested feature sets.
models_and_equal_budget.secondary_model: A fixed-gradient boosted-tree model may be reported only as a robustness analysis if preregistered before result unblinding, using an identical hyperparameter budget across ladders.
models_and_equal_budget.selection_rule: Select the penalty using the fixed July development set by scalar aggregate loss. Ties within 0.001 standardized loss select the larger penalty.

feature_negative_controls: Randomly permuted versions of temporal features, permuted within training data only.
Features computed from an earlier non-overlapping historical window that should be weakly related to immediate future change.
Stable bookkeeping summaries expected to contain no incremental temporal or structural signal after M0.
negative_controls.interpretation: Negative-control failure does not prove validity, but large apparent gains from null-control features would trigger a pipeline audit.
negative_controls.status: Negative-control definitions must be frozen before model fitting; they are not part of the primary claim.
target_negative_controls: A shifted future window beginning at t+60d, only if complete observation is available and the analysis is preregistered before unblinding.
A fixed pseudo-target created from an earlier historical interval, used only to detect pipeline artifacts.

bootstrap.method: Cluster bootstrap with replacement over eligible wallets; retain all rows for each sampled wallet.
bootstrap.reason: Preserves within-wallet dependence and avoids treating repeated observations as independent.
bootstrap.unit: Wallet cluster within the August cutoff.

null_hypotheses_and_resampling.confidence_intervals: Use 95% confidence intervals for paired test-row loss differences.
null_hypotheses_and_resampling.effective_sample_size: Report wallet count, row count, repeated-wallet proportion, and cluster-robust uncertainty.
null_hypotheses: M1 provides no incremental predictive utility over M0.
M2_CORE provides no incremental predictive utility over M1.
M2_CORE provides no incremental predictive utility over M0.

permutation_test.method: Permute model prediction vectors across wallet clusters within the August test set, preserving target vectors and cluster membership.
permutation_test.warning: Permutation inference is not a substitute for temporal validation and is reported only as a robustness check.

null_hypotheses_and_resampling.small_cluster_rule: If the unseen-wallet stratum has fewer than 500 wallets, do not use nominal formal testing for that stratum.

primary_secondary_metrics.multiplicity: Use Holm adjustment for the three primary nested comparisons if formal claims are made for all three. The M1 versus M0 comparison is the first-priority contrast.

primary_metric.comparison: Report paired loss differences M1 minus M0, M2_CORE minus M1, and M2_CORE minus M0 on the same August rows.
primary_metric.definition: Mean squared error averaged equally across target dimensions after training-only target standardization.
primary_metric.name: Multivariate standardized mean squared error

primary_scalar_summary.definition: (Loss_baseline - Loss_model) divided by Loss_baseline, with the baseline specified separately for each comparison.
primary_scalar_summary.name: Relative loss reduction

primary_secondary_metrics.reporting_rule: The primary conclusion is based on the prespecified multivariate loss and its paired confidence interval; secondary metrics are descriptive or multiplicity-adjusted.
secondary_metrics: Rank correlation between predicted and observed scalar surprise
Calibration slope and intercept for the scalar surprise
Loss by repeated-wallet and unseen-wallet strata
primary_secondary_metrics.threshold_status: Metric definitions and multiplicity rules are pre-analysis choices.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Compare nested gains to M0 and report activity-stratified results.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The apparent gain reflects historical activity scale rather than temporal or structural organization.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Compare repeated-wallet and unseen-wallet performance without using identity as a feature.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The result reflects repeated-wallet memorization or stable wallet-specific behavior.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Run fixed-horizon completeness checks and report exclusions by cutoff.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The result is caused by incomplete or unequal future observation.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Run key uniqueness, UTC, row-count conservation, and timestamp-boundary audits.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The result is caused by join duplication or timestamp misalignment.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Verify immutable July-only tuning logs and one-time August evaluation.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The result is a consequence of tuning on the test cutoff.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Use wallet-cluster bootstrap intervals and fixed activity strata.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The result is concentrated in a few high-activity wallets.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Report composition and directional dimensions separately and compare against the no-change reference baseline.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The target is mainly future activity level rather than behavioral change.

strongest_alternative_explanations.diagnostic: Treat the result as a bounded pilot and require additional preregistered cutoffs for confirmation.
strongest_alternative_explanations.explanation: The apparent effect is an artifact of a single temporal transition.

active_days.reason: Captures persistence without dividing by an endogenous future denominator.
active_days.transform: Raw count over the fixed future window, standardized using training data.

directional_shares.reason: Prevents undefined values for all-zero or single-category windows.
directional_shares.transform: Additive-smoothed proportions using 0.5 pseudo-events per category.

event_count.reason: Reduces extreme right skew while retaining zero values.

event_family_composition.reason: Avoids exact linear dependence among all shares.
event_family_composition.transform: Additive-smoothed category shares, represented by three contrasts against a reference family.

target_missingness.rule: Exclude only dimensions that fail a documented source-completeness check; report dimension-specific denominators and do not use model-based future imputation.

unique_counterparties.reason: Reduces scale domination and preserves zero values.

zero_activity_future_windows.rule: Retain rows and represent zero counts explicitly; do not condition the primary analysis on future activity.

temporal_train_dev_test_protocol.amendment_requirement: Adding cutoffs requires a preregistered amendment before inspecting results, with a new fixed train-development-test schedule.

repeated_wallet_evaluation.definition: August wallets that also appear at June or July.
repeated_wallet_evaluation.leakage_control: Wallet identity is not a feature, and all preprocessing remains time-fitted.
repeated_wallet_evaluation.purpose: Measures within-wallet temporal forecasting under expected repeated observations.

temporal_train_dev_test_protocol.three_cutoff_limitation: There is only one strictly held-out future cutoff, so the August result is a single temporal replication point rather than a robust estimate across many dates.

unseen_wallet_evaluation.analysis_rule: Report as a prespecified secondary analysis, not as the primary estimand.
unseen_wallet_evaluation.definition: August wallets absent from both June and July rows.
unseen_wallet_evaluation.minimum_size_rule: If fewer than 500 eligible August wallets remain, report descriptively without formal significance testing. This threshold is a pre-analysis design choice.

temporal_train_dev_test_protocol.within_earlier_period_validation: Do not randomly split wallet-cutoff rows. If an internal fit diagnostic is required, use a wallet-clustered blocked split within June only, with no use of July or August outcomes.
workflow: Fit preprocessing and candidate models on June only.
Use July only for selecting among the frozen hyperparameter grid and checking implementation stability.
Refit the selected specification on June and July together using only pre-August information.
Evaluate once on August and freeze the test predictions and test metrics before any exploratory subgroup analysis.
